account: On the evening of 25 September 2021, Muhammad Fitri, 24, was riding home when a gray van struck his motorcycle. That was at the junction of Ang Mo Kio Avenue 6 and Ang Mo Kio Street 31, Singapore. The driver fled; Fitri lost consciousness on a near-empty road. His Apple Watch's Fall Detection registered the impact. Via the paired phone it automatically called an ambulance and texted and phoned his emergency contact, his girlfriend. The Singapore Civil Defence Force said it was alerted around 8:20pm. Fitri was regaining consciousness as paramedics arrived. He was conveyed, conscious, to Khoo Teck Puat Hospital with abrasions, a neck collar and a suspected bleed at the back of the head. Police confirmed a hit-and-run.

ai_role.statement: The watch's fall-detection classifier read the collision's impact as a hard fall. With the wearer unresponsive, it placed the automatic ambulance call through the paired phone and sent the location texts and calls to his girlfriend. SCDF paramedics treated and conveyed him. The counterfactual is unproven. A passer-by later picked up his phone and spoke to the girlfriend. The family at first assumed that person had called the ambulance, and Fitri was regaining consciousness as paramedics arrived.

fields.account: On the evening of 25 September 2021, Muhammad Fitri, 24, was riding home when a gray van struck his motorcycle. That was at the junction of Ang Mo Kio Avenue 6 and Ang Mo Kio Street 31, Singapore. The driver fled; Fitri lost consciousness on a near-empty road. His Apple Watch's Fall Detection registered the impact. Via the paired phone it automatically called an ambulance and texted and phoned his emergency contact, his girlfriend. The Singapore Civil Defence Force said it was alerted around 8:20pm. Fitri was regaining consciousness as paramedics arrived. He was conveyed, conscious, to Khoo Teck Puat Hospital with abrasions, a neck collar and a suspected bleed at the back of the head. Police confirmed a hit-and-run.
